strengths: The structural stall reads clearly through its striped physical canopy, timber frame, counter, lower stock shelf and hanging price board.
Produce baskets contain individually modelled mixed inventory and retain a distinct silhouette from the tied provision sacks.
Authored metre-space cluster offsets now place physical baskets on the 1.09 metre counter and sacks on the lower shelf in both unrelated hosts.
All ten entities per transfer remain fully inspectable across three distinct landmarks while customer and entrance circulation remain clear.
limitations: Accepted for background and medium shots only; basket weave and burlap fibres are procedural surface responses rather than close-up textile construction.
The provision sack uses deterministic gathered seams and a cinched profile rather than dynamic cloth simulation.
The host scenes prove transfer and circulation semantics but are verification fixtures, not publishable finished market environments.
notes: V1 was rejected because the sacks read as smooth ceramic jars and the stall lacked a merchandising focal cue. V2 added coarse burlap response, raised gathered seams, and a physical price board, but fail-closed acceptance exposed inconsistent vertical cluster-offset scaling that embedded the baskets below their authored counter anchors. V3 fixes that solver defect and is accepted only at its declared medium/background tier.
